chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Habib al-Kha'thami from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man has wealth in his possession as a trust (deposit); may he take from it without the owner's permission? He said: 'He does not take unless he has 'afā' (ability to compensate/replace it).'
I said: What if he finds someone to guarantee it for him, but he himself does not have 'afā', and the one who guarantees it testifies on his behalf? Will he take from it? He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.وَفَاء: Ability to compensate or replace the value

ai.seo_question: Can a trustee use deposited money without the owner's permission if he provides a guarantor?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *riju'* (using deposited wealth) by establishing that a trustee may use the funds if he possesses *wafā'* (financial solvency to guarantee replacement). The discussion extends to cases where personal solvency is insufficient, allowing the use of a third-party guarantor (*dāmin*) whose testimony secures the owner's right, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on risk mitigation in trust contracts. This ruling highlights the balance between facilitating economic utility for the trustee and protecting the depositor's capital from loss.
